lines.t: Hi! Can I get a cup of tea, please?
Sure. Would you like milk and sugar?
Milk, but no sugar, please.
Anything else?
Yes, one chicken sandwich.
That's two hundred and fifty taka.
Here you go. Thank you!

q.s: How does A want the tea?
What food does A order?
How much is it in total?

lines.t: Hello! Are you new here?
Yes, I moved in last week. I'm Rahim.
Nice to meet you, Rahim. I'm Sara. I live on the third floor.
Nice to meet you too. Do you work nearby?
Yes, I'm a teacher at the school across the road.
That's great. See you around!

q.s: When did Rahim move in?
Which floor does Sara live on?
What is Sara's job?

lines.t: Excuse me, how do I get to the bus station?
Go straight for about five minutes, then turn right.
Is it near the big mosque?
Yes, it's just opposite the mosque.
Thank you so much!
You're welcome.

q.s: How long should A go straight at first?
Which way should A turn after that?
Where is the bus station?

lines.t: Good morning, City Clinic. How can I help you?
Hi, I'd like to book an appointment with Doctor Hasan.
Sure. Is Thursday at four o'clock okay?
Sorry, I work until five on Thursday. Do you have anything on Saturday?
Yes, Saturday at eleven in the morning.
Perfect. My name is Rahim Ahmed.
Thank you, Mr. Ahmed. See you on Saturday.

q.s: Which doctor does A want to see?
Why can't A come on Thursday?
o: A will be out of Dhaka

q.s: When is the appointment in the end?

lines.t: Can I help you?
Yes, I'm looking for a blue shirt.
What size are you?
Medium, I think.
Here's one. It's on sale today, only eight hundred taka.
Can I try it on?
Of course. The changing room is over there.
It fits well. I'll take it.

q.s: What color shirt is A looking for?
How much is the shirt?
What does A do in the end?

lines.t: What are you doing this weekend?
I'm going to visit my grandparents in the village.
That sounds nice. How are you going there?
By train. It takes about four hours.
When are you coming back?
On Sunday evening. What about you?
I'm going to stay home and study for my exam.

q.s: Where is B going?
How is B travelling?
What will A do at the weekend?
o: Stay home and study for an exam

lines.t: Hello, Pizza Corner. What would you like?
I'd like one large chicken pizza, please.
Anything to drink?
Two bottles of water.
Okay. What's your address?
House twelve, Road five, Mirpur ten.
It will take about forty minutes.

q.s: What does A order?
Where does A live?
How long will the food take?

lines.t: Hello, I have a booking under the name Rahim.
Welcome, sir. Yes, a single room for two nights.
Is breakfast included?
Yes, breakfast is from seven to ten in the restaurant.
Great. What's the Wi-Fi password?
It's on your key card. Your room is three oh five, on the third floor.

q.s: How many nights is the booking for?
When is breakfast served?
What is the room number?

lines.t: So, tell me a little about yourself.
I'm a web developer with four years of experience. I mostly build websites for small businesses.
Why do you want to join our company?
I like your projects, and I want to work in a bigger team and learn new skills.
What is your biggest strength?
I'm good at solving problems, and I always try to finish my work on time.

q.s: How many years of experience does A have?

q.sbn: সে কেন এই কোম্পানিতে আসতে চায়?
obn: বড় দলে কাজ করে নতুন দক্ষতা শিখতে
q.s: Why does A want to join the company?
o: To work in a bigger team and learn new skills
Because the office is near home

obn: সমস্যার সমাধান আর সময়মতো কাজ শেষ করা
q.s: What is A's biggest strength?
o: Solving problems and finishing work on time

lines.t: Hi, thanks for joining. Can you hear me?
Yes, loud and clear. So, what do you need help with?
Our website is very slow, and we are losing customers.
I see. I can check the speed and send you a report by tomorrow.
That would be great. How much will it cost?
The report is free. If you want me to fix it, I'll send you a price after that.

q.s: What is the client's problem?
When will A send the report?
How much does the report cost?

lines.t: You're late again. Is everything okay?
I'm really sorry. There was a huge traffic jam because of an accident.
I understand, but the client meeting started at nine.
I know. Can I join now, or should I wait?
Join now. And next time, please send me a message if you're running late.
Of course. It won't happen again.

q.s: Why was A late?
o: A big traffic jam after an accident

q.s: What time did the client meeting start?

q.sbn: পরের বার কী করতে বলা হলো?
q.s: What should A do next time?
o: Send a message if running late

lines.t: Hi, I bought these headphones last week, but the left side doesn't work.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt?
Yes, here it is.
Thank you. Would you like a new pair or your money back?
A new pair, please.
No problem. Let me check if we have them in stock.

q.s: What is wrong with the headphones?
What does the shop assistant ask for?
What does A want in the end?

lines.t: Thanks for making time today. I wanted to talk about the launch date.
Sure. Is everything still on track for the fifteenth?
Mostly, yes, but the payment pages are taking longer than we expected.
That's a bit worrying. What exactly is causing the delay?
Your payment provider changed its system last week, so we have to rebuild part of the checkout.
I see. So what are you suggesting?
We could launch on the fifteenth without online payments, or move the whole launch to the twenty-second.
Hmm. Launching without payments doesn't really make sense for us.
I agree. If we move the date, I can promise everything will be fully tested.
All right, let's go with the twenty-second. But please keep me updated every Friday.
Absolutely. I'll send you a short progress report every Friday afternoon.

q.s: Why is the project late?
o: The payment provider changed its system

q.s: What does the client decide?
o: To launch on the 15th without payments

q.s: What does A promise to do?
o: Send a progress report every Friday

lines.t: Good afternoon, Swift Delivery customer support. How can I help?
Hi. I ordered a laptop ten days ago, and it still hasn't arrived. The website said three to five days.
I'm sorry about that. Could you give me your order number, please?
Yes, it's four, eight, two, seven, one.
Thank you. It looks like the parcel was sent to our Chittagong office by mistake.
Chittagong? I live in Dhaka. I needed it for work this week.
I completely understand. I can arrange express delivery, and it should reach you tomorrow before noon.
Tomorrow is fine. But honestly, I'm not happy about this delay.
Of course. As an apology, we'll refund your delivery charge.
Thank you. Could you also send me a text when it's on the way?
Certainly. You'll get a message with the driver's number in the morning.

q.s: Where was the parcel sent by mistake?
q.sbn: পার্সেলটা ভুল করে কোথায় পাঠানো হয়েছিল?

q.s: When will the laptop arrive?
What will the company do to say sorry?
q.sbn: দুঃখ প্রকাশ করতে কোম্পানি কী করবে?

lines.t: So, we've got a budget of fifty thousand taka for the end-of-year event. Any ideas?
Last year we just had dinner at a restaurant. People said it felt a bit boring.
True. What about a day trip instead? Somewhere outside the city.
That could work, but some people won't want to travel for hours.
Fair point. How about a place close to Dhaka, maybe an hour away, with games and lunch included?
I like that. We could also do a small award ceremony in the afternoon.
Good idea. Should we ask the team first, though? I don't want to decide everything ourselves.
Let's send a quick survey with two or three options and a deadline of Thursday.
Perfect. I'll write the survey today, and you can check the prices.
Deal. I'll call a few resorts tomorrow morning.

q.s: Why do they want something different this year?
q.sbn: এবার তারা অন্যরকম কিছু চায় কেন?

q.s: How will they decide?
o: By sending a survey to the team

q.s: What will B do tomorrow?

lines.t: Thanks for coming in. I'd like to start with what went well this year.
Sure. I'm keen to hear your feedback.
Your work on the client portal was outstanding. The client specifically mentioned how responsive you were.
That's great to hear. It was a demanding project, but I learned a lot.
It showed. On the other hand, a few internal deadlines slipped, especially in the summer.
That's fair. I took on too much at once and didn't flag it early enough.
Exactly. Next year, I'd like you to raise concerns as soon as you see a risk, rather than waiting.
Understood. Would it help if I shared a short weekly status update with you?
That would be really helpful. And I'd also like you to start mentoring one of the junior developers.
I'd be happy to. I've actually been hoping for a chance to lead more.
Good. Let's put both of those in your goals for next year.

q.s: What did the client praise?
What problem does the manager mention?
o: A was often late to work
A made mistakes in the code

q.s: What new responsibility will A take on?

lines.t: In short, our app connects small farmers directly with restaurants in the city, so both sides get a fairer price.
Interesting. But plenty of delivery apps already exist. What makes yours different?
Most of them focus on consumers. We focus on businesses, and we handle quality checks before anything is delivered.
How do you make money?
We take a seven percent fee on each order, and restaurants can pay for a premium plan with faster delivery.
And how many customers do you have so far?
We ran a three-month pilot with twelve restaurants, and nine of them have already signed annual contracts.
That's a solid start. What's the biggest risk you see?
Honestly, logistics. Keeping vegetables fresh on long journeys is expensive, so we're testing cold boxes with a local partner.
I appreciate the honesty. Send me your financial projections, and let's talk again next week.

q.s: Who does the app mainly connect?
q.sbn: অ্যাপটা মূলত কাদের মধ্যে যোগাযোগ করায়?

q.s: How did the pilot go?
o: Nine of the twelve restaurants signed contracts

q.s: What does A see as the biggest risk?
q.sbn: A সবচেয়ে বড় ঝুঁকি কোনটাকে মনে করে?

lines.t: I honestly don't know how you work from home every day. I'd go crazy.
It took some getting used to, I'll admit. But I save nearly three hours of commuting.
Sure, but don't you miss the people? Half of what I learn comes from overhearing colleagues.
That's a fair point. Junior staff probably lose out the most when everyone is remote.
Exactly. And it's harder to switch off when your office is your bedroom.
True, which is why I set strict hours and keep my laptop out of the bedroom.
So would you never go back to the office?
I wouldn't say never. I think two days in the office and three at home would be ideal.
Now that I could live with. Collaboration days and focus days.
Precisely. It's not really about where we work, but about what kind of work we're doing.

q.s: What does A save by working from home?
o: A lot of money on lunch
q.sbn: বাসা থেকে কাজ করে A কী বাঁচায়?

q.s: Who does A think loses out most from remote work?
q.sbn: A-এর মতে রিমোট কাজে সবচেয়ে বেশি ক্ষতি কার?

q.s: What does A think would be ideal?
o: Two office days and three home days
Going back to the office full time
obn: সপ্তাহে দুই দিন অফিস, তিন দিন বাসা
